Its borate chemistry is more oxidation-tolerant than sulfides, which should help at 4.0 V against LiCoO2.
proposals.motivation: Earlier Li3PO4 (phosphate, Li-rich, wide-gap) was evaluated; this moves to the borate family with a similar Li-rich, insulating profile to test whether a different anion chemistry gives a lower interfacial penalty.

proposals.hypothesis: Li6Ti2O7 is a Li-rich titanate with d0 Ti4+ and O2-, so it has no reducible transition-metal cation that could be oxidized or reduced at the 4.0 V interface. Its band gap should be well above 2 eV, so it should be an electronic insulator. The high Li content should limit Li depletion at the LiCoO2 interface, and its oxide chemistry should be reasonably compatible with Li6PS5Cl. This is a titanate family not yet sampled, unlike the phosphate, borate, halide, simple-oxide and silicate coatings already tested.
proposals.motivation: Earlier coatings covered phosphate, borate, fluoride, simple-oxide and silicate chemistries, but no titanate. Li6Ti2O7 tests a Li-rich d0 titanate, which is the first new oxide family in the set.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (~6 eV) lithium-rich phosphate that is a good electronic insulator. It is a well-known coating for oxide cathodes and sulfide electrolytes: it is chemically compatible with Li6PS5Cl and has a moderate, reasonably stable interface with LiCoO2 at 4.0 V. Its Li-rich composition should also limit Li-ion depletion at the interfaces.

Li3BO3 is a Li-rich, wide-gap orthoborate with good electronic insulation. Its high Li content should limit Li depletion at the interface, and it is reported as a chemically compatible coating for both oxide cathodes and sulfide electrolytes such as Li6PS5Cl. Its borate chemistry is more oxidation-tolerant than sulfides, which should help at 4.0 V against LiCoO2.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li3PO4 (phosphate, Li-rich, wide-gap) was evaluated; this moves to the borate family with a similar Li-rich, insulating profile to test whether a different anion chemistry gives a lower interfacial penalty.

proposal.hypothesis: LiF is a very wide-gap (~14 eV), electrochemically stable Li-rich fluoride that is an electronic insulator. It is a classic protective coating for oxide cathodes, with low reactivity toward LiCoO2 at 4.0 V. Its fluoride chemistry differs from the earlier phosphate and borate coatings, and it should be chemically compatible with Li6PS5Cl, so it tests a new anion family.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li3PO4 (phosphate) and Li3BO3 (borate) were both Li-rich, wide-gap oxyanion coatings. LiF moves to the halide family to check whether a non-oxyanion, highly insulating and oxidation-stable interlayer gives a lower interfacial penalty.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2O is a very Li-rich, wide-gap (~5 eV) oxide and a pure oxide with no oxyanion or reducible transition-metal cation. It should be a good electronic insulator, and its high Li content should limit Li depletion at the LiCoO2 interface. It is also expected to be chemically compatible with Li6PS5Cl. This tests a simple oxide family not yet sampled.

Li8ZrO6 is a very Li-rich, d0 Zr4+ oxide with a wide band gap and no reducible transition-metal cation, so it should be an electronic insulator and oxidation-stable against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V. Its high Li content should limit Li depletion at the interface, and its oxide chemistry should be reasonably compatible with Li6PS5Cl. It is a different family from the phosphate and borate coatings already tested.

Li8SiO6 is a very Li-rich orthosilicate built from d0 Si4+ and O2-, with no reducible transition-metal cation. It should be a wide-gap electronic insulator and oxidation-stable against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V. Its high Li content should limit Li depletion at the interface. The silicate family has not been sampled yet, so this tests a new oxyanion chemistry alongside the earlier phosphate, borate, fluoride and oxide coatings.
proposal.motivation: Earlier coatings (Li3PO4, Li3BO3, LiF, Li2O, Li8ZrO6) covered phosphate, borate, halide and simple oxide families, but none was silicate. Li8SiO6 is the Li-richest silicate available and fits the same insulating, Li-rich profile.

proposal.hypothesis: Li5Al(SiO4)2 is a Li-rich aluminosilicate built from Al3+ and Si4+ (both d0 or closed-shell) with no reducible transition-metal cation. It should be a wide-gap electronic insulator and oxidation-stable against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V. Its high Li content should limit Li depletion at the interface, and its oxide chemistry should be reasonably compatible with Li6PS5Cl.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li8SiO6 (silicate, Li-rich, insulating) was evaluated. Li5Al(SiO4)2 stays in the silicate family but adds Al3+ to lower Li-content-driven reactivity and test whether a more stable aluminosilicate lowers the interfacial penalty.
